notable_absence.finding: This page never states who is allowed to run cbbackupmgr - no role, privilege, or RBAC mention anywhere on the tool's own overview/architecture page. That fact appears only on enterprise-backup-restore.md ('Only Full Administrators can use cbbackupmgr') and, in a narrower bucket-level form, on cbbackupmgr-backup.md's own RBAC section (the data_backup role). The architecture page that a reader would naturally start from supplies no access-control fact at all.

cross_component_finding: This page states plainly, in its own AUTHORS section, 'cbbackupmgr is a Couchbase Enterprise Edition tool and was written by Couchbase.' The sibling page enterprise-backup-restore.md - despite being titled 'cbbackupmgr' and sitting in the same backup-restore/ module - states the opposite: 'Only Full Administrators can use `cbbackupmgr`; which is available for both Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition and Couchbase Server Community Edition.' One page in this exact module asserts the whole tool is Enterprise-only; the other asserts it ships in both editions. Both statements are quoted verbatim, from two pages that link to each other. This is a direct within-module contradiction on the single most consequential edition-gating fact this round was dispatched to look for.
